title: Journey Inventory
description: The registry of all business journeys in the organisation. A journey is a discrete end-to-end scenario in which a persona achieves a goal by exercising one or more capabilities. Journeys are the primary unit of behavioural modelling and the thing against which an organisation delivers. The inventory is a flat list: each entry summarises a journey and references the capabilities and sub-capabilities it exercises.

document_version.description: Semantic version of this inventory document.

recommended_first_journey.description: Optional. The journey an event-storming programme should model first. Usually chosen because it establishes the foundational domain entities the greatest number of other journeys depend on.

id.description: JRN-XXX reference to a journey in the journeys array.

rationale.description: Why this journey should be modelled first.

journeys.description: All identified business journeys. Ordering is informational; use priority and depends_on_journeys for sequencing decisions.

description.description: One to three sentence explanation of the journey scope: who, what, and why. Includes the regulatory or commercial driver where material.

triggering_persona.description: The primary persona who initiates the journey. References a persona ID.

capabilities_touched.description: Top-level capabilities exercised by this journey. At least one required.

sub_capabilities_involved.description: Sub-capabilities exercised by this journey. Each must belong to one of the capabilities in capabilities_touched.

cross_capability.description: True if the journey exercises sub-capabilities from two or more top-level capabilities. Validators should enforce consistency with capabilities_touched.

priority.description: Delivery priority tier. critical = the organisation cannot legally or operationally function without it; high = significant commercial or regulatory weight; medium = material but not blocking; low = deferrable without consequence.

priority_rationale.description: Explanation of the priority assignment, citing the specific driver.

estimated_complexity.description: Indicative complexity for modelling-workshop planning. simple = single capability, linear happy path; moderate = 1-2 capabilities, branching; complex = multi-capability, significant branching, real-time or regulatory constraints.

happy_path_summary.description: A terse numbered-step or prose description of the successful end-to-end flow, sufficient to orient a modelling facilitator.

depends_on_journeys.description: Other journeys that must be modelled first because they establish domain entities or aggregate roots this journey references. Empty array means no prerequisites. This is a modelling dependency, not a technical runtime dependency.
